steps.name: Blocked DESeq2 LRT and pairwise Wald contrasts
caveats: 4 subjects per condition is at the low end for RNA-seq; effect estimates for low-count genes are noisy even after shrinkage

A null result for treated_b vs treated_a is not evidence that the two treatments are equivalent
steps.context: Complete paired design, 4 subjects x 3 conditions, 12 samples, human. The subject term removes between-subject variance so every comparison is made within subject. Counts came from Salmon; the profile provides only a gene-level count matrix, so no transcript-length offsets are available. This must be stated: without tximport length offsets a gene whose isoform usage shifts can be mis-called, and the plain integer matrix is used as given.
steps.question: Which genes change in ANY condition within a subject (LRT of ~subject+condition vs ~subject), and for each of treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, and treated_b vs treated_a, which genes change and by how much?

Plot the unadjusted p-value histogram for the LRT and for each contrast before trusting the adjusted values. steps.context: Human blood data. The environment census shows human hallmark, human canonical pathways (KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID), human GO and human WikiPathways collections staged as symbol GMTs. Resolve what is actually present at run time; if a Reactome-specific collection is not there, use the staged human canonical-pathway collection in its place and name what was used. Hallmark alone still answers the question, so the loss of a follow-up collection costs annotation depth, not the step.
steps.question: Which Hallmark, Reactome and WikiPathways gene sets are coordinately shifted in treated_a vs control, in treated_b vs control, and between treated_b and treated_a?

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on the full tested list is the default enrichment (R-0107), hallmark first then Reactome/WikiPathways for human (R-0048, R-0098, R-0165), one run per contrast (R-0104); the disputed ranking metric (R-0108) is settled in favour of the DESeq2 Wald statistic per R-0099.

constraints: Rank by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat). This resolves the disputed ranking-metric choice: the Wald statistic is signed and scaled by its own standard error, unlike the unshrunken log2 fold change, and does not saturate into ties like a signed p-value. State this choice in the output

Gene set size window 15 to 500 applied AFTER intersecting each set with the tested genes
Run enrichment once per contrast; never pool genes from several contrasts into one list

For any over-representation test the universe is exactly the genes tested in T1S2, never the whole genome or annotation
Do not run ORA on a list of fewer than about 50 significant genes; report the list size instead
Use human gene-set collections only — the store also holds mouse and rat collections and a species mismatch fails silently as an empty result
Set and record a random seed for the fgsea permutations

Keep gene sets with 15 to 500 members after intersection with the tested genes. Apply BH within each collection and each contrast, collapse redundant significant sets and report one representative per group, and record the leading-edge genes of each significant set with their Wald statistics. One results table per contrast per collection, each labelled with the contrast name and the collection name and release

steps.name: Integrated report
caveats: No transcript-level data was provided, so nothing in this report addresses isoform switching

Blood transcriptomes are strongly shaped by cell composition; a differential gene may reflect a shift in cell proportions rather than a within-cell change, and this cannot be resolved from the gene-level matrix alone
steps.context: Final synthesis across T1S2 (model), T1S3 (method overlap) and T2S1 (enrichment). The report is the artifact the user reads, so the power limits of a 4-subject design belong in it explicitly rather than in a footnote.
steps.question: What is the consolidated, reproducible answer: which genes respond to either treatment within subject, which are specific to treated_a or treated_b, do the two treatments differ, and how confident can the reader be given 4 subjects?

grounding.reason: Report contents follow the procedure's report step: method/design/thresholds (R-0041), shrunken and unshrunken effects with ranking on the shrunken value (R-0085), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), two-method overlap (R-0042), enrichment provenance and leading edge (R-0051, R-0105), and the reproducibility record (R-0086).

constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep p-values from the unshrunken fit
Report the FDR as holding within each contrast, not across the set of contrasts
Do not present the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the result
Do not claim a mechanism from an enriched gene set; present sets as hypotheses
State the number of Cook's-distance-flagged NA genes separately from independent-filter NAs
steps.description: Assemble the differential expression and enrichment outputs into one report. plan.title: Paired 3-arm blood RNA-seq: treated_a/treated_b vs control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a gene-symbol x sample raw count matrix from Salmon (12,000 genes x 12 samples, counts.csv) with a 12 x 3 sample table (metadata.csv) giving subject and condition. Four subjects each contribute one control, one treated_a and one treated_b sample — a complete within-subject block over three conditions, single batch, human whole blood. The research question has two halves: (1) which genes respond to either treatment within a subject, and (2) whether the two treatments differ from each other. Both are answered by one model that carries subject as a blocking term: full ~ subject + condition against reduced ~ subject.

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC on the blind VST — PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes — coloured by condition and by subject. With paired blood samples the expected picture is that subject, not condition, drives PC1; that is not a defect but it must be seen before the model is trusted, and it is also where a swapped subject label or a low-depth library would show.

T1S2 fits the model. The DESeq2 LRT (~subject + condition vs ~subject) answers the 'responds to either treatment' half directly as a single 2-degrees-of-freedom test per gene, which is more powerful than taking the union of two pairwise lists. The three pairwise Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_b vs treated_a) answer 'which treatment' and 'do they differ'. control is set explicitly as the reference level; treated_b vs treated_a is a contrast of two non-reference coefficients, so its LFC is shrunk with ashr rather than apeglm. BH is applied within each contrast and the LRT separately, and the per-contrast p-value histogram is inspected first. n=4 subjects is small: DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and returns NA p-values rather than replacing counts at this replicate level, and those NAs must be reported apart from the independent-filter NAs.

T1S3 is the robustness check the design deserves at n=4: the same blocked design refit with edgeR quasi-likelihood (glmQLFit, with an ANOVA-like test across the two treatment coefficients matching the LRT, and the three matching contrasts). The intersection of the two methods is the high-confidence set; genes called by one method only are reported separately with the method named. This is a sanity check on the inference, not a second chance at significance.

T2S1 runs fgsea preranked on the full ranked list of tested genes for each of the three Wald contrasts, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the disputed ranking choice is settled here in favour of the Wald statistic — signed and scaled by its own standard error, which the unshrunken LFC is not). Hallmark is the first pass, Reactome/WikiPathways the follow-up, one table per contrast, never pooled across contrasts. The LRT has no signed statistic and so gets no preranked test; if its significant set is large enough (>=50 genes) an over-representation test against the tested-gene universe is run, otherwise the step reports the list size and skips ORA.

T1S4 assembles the report: design, reference level, every contrast by name, thresholds, gene counts, MA and dispersion plots, both shrunken and unshrunken LFC with lfcSE, leading-edge genes per significant set, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, and the reproducibility record.

Power caveat stated up front: four subjects per condition is at the low end for RNA-seq. The pairing buys back real power by removing between-subject variance, but a null result for treated_b vs treated_a is weak evidence of equivalence, not evidence of no difference, and every step is instructed to say so.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes
Low count filter: at least 10 counts in at least 4 samples
~ subject + condition with control as reference level
DESeq2 likelihood ratio test then pairwise Wald contrasts
fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome/WikiPathways
Reproducible report with fit diagnostics, effect columns, leading edge, session info

grounding.reason: Paired design over three conditions: subject as a fixed block with the DESeq2 LRT (~subject+condition vs ~subject) then per-level Wald contrasts (R-0069, R-0011); ashr shrinkage because treated_b vs treated_a is not a single coefficient (R-0040); explicit reference level and named contrasts (R-0060, R-0036); BH within contrast (R-0061). The knowledge check warned that reference_level should be 'explicit' — control is named explicitly here, which satisfies the rule.

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood cross-check
steps.question: Do the genes called as treatment-responsive by DESeq2 hold up under an independent count model — edgeR quasi-likelihood with the same ~ subject + condition design — and how large is the intersection?
steps.description: Refit the same filtered count matrix with edgeR: DGEList, TMM normalization factors, model.matrix(~ subject + condition) with control as the reference level, estimateDisp and glmQLFit. Run glmQLFTest across the two condition coefficients jointly (the edgeR analogue of the DESeq2 LRT) and on each of the three contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_b vs treated_a) using makeContrasts. Apply BH within each test. Then compare against the DESeq2 tables from T1S2: report per test the number significant by each method, the size of the intersection, and the genes called by exactly one method with that method named. Write the intersection as the high-confidence gene set.
steps.context: At 4 replicates per group DESeq2 and edgeR agree on most genes but each calls some the other does not, and the disagreement is largest at low counts and low replicate numbers. This step exists to size that disagreement on this dataset rather than to add discoveries. The union is never the result.
acceptance_criteria: edgeR QL fit completed on the identical filtered gene set and the identical ~ subject + condition design with control as reference
Per test (any-treatment, treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_b vs treated_a): n significant by DESeq2, n by edgeR, and n in the intersection
High-confidence intersection gene set written to file per test
Method-specific genes listed separately with the calling method named; the union is explicitly NOT presented as the result
constraints: Use the same pre-filtered gene set and the same design matrix as T1S2 so the comparison is like for like
TMM normalization factors go inside the edgeR model; do not pre-normalize the counts
BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 within each test
Report the intersection as the high-confidence set and never the union
caveats: Two methods agreeing does not make a gene biologically real — it makes the statistical call robust to model choice
Disagreement concentrated at low counts is the expected pattern and should be described, not treated as an error

grounding.reason: R-0042 requires the DESeq2/edgeR-QL overlap as the robustness report at these replicate numbers, and R-0001 names edgeR QL as the co-equal method at 2-11 replicates per group.

steps.name: Preranked GSEA per contrast
steps.question: Which Hallmark, Reactome and WikiPathways gene sets are coordinately shifted in treated_a vs control, in treated_b vs control, and between treated_b and treated_a?
steps.description: For each of the three Wald contrasts from T1S2, build a ranked list of ALL tested genes ordered by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the stat column) and run fgsea against three human gene-set collections separately: MSigDB hallmark first, then a Reactome-style curated canonical-pathway collection and the human WikiPathways collection as follow-ups. Keep gene sets with 15 to 500 members after intersection with the tested genes. Apply BH within each collection and each contrast, collapse redundant significant sets and report one representative per group, and record the leading-edge genes of each significant set with their Wald statistics. Produce one table per contrast per collection — never pooled. Separately, take the LRT-significant gene set from T1S2: if it contains at least 50 genes, run an over-representation test against a universe of exactly the genes tested in T1S2; if it is smaller, skip the ORA and state the list size and the reason. Row identifiers in the count matrix are HGNC gene symbols and the staged collections are symbol-based, so no Entrez mapping is required; report the share of ranked genes that matched no set as the equivalent diagnostic, and if an identifier mapping is used anywhere report the unmapped share.
steps.context: Human blood data. Needed reference data: human hallmark gene sets, a human curated canonical-pathway collection of Reactome type, and human WikiPathways — all as symbol-keyed gene-set collections. The environment census shows human hallmark, human canonical pathways (KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID), human GO and human WikiPathways collections staged as symbol GMTs. Resolve what is actually present at run time; if a Reactome-specific collection is not there, use the staged human canonical-pathway collection in its place and name what was used. Hallmark alone still answers the question, so the loss of a follow-up collection costs annotation depth, not the step.
acceptance_criteria: Three ranked lists built, one per contrast, each containing every gene tested in T1S2 with no significance cutoff applied before ranking
fgsea run per contrast per collection with minSize 15 and maxSize 500 and a fixed random seed recorded
One results table per contrast per collection, each labelled with the contrast name and the collection name and release
Redundant significant sets collapsed with one representative reported per group; the full table kept as a supplement
Leading-edge genes listed for each significant set together with their Wald statistics
LRT gene list: either an ORA run against the tested-gene universe with the universe size stated, or an explicit statement that the list held fewer than 50 genes and ORA was skipped
The name and release of every gene-set collection actually used is recorded; if a planned collection was absent at run time that is stated rather than silently substituted
constraints: Rank by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat). This resolves the disputed ranking-metric choice: the Wald statistic is signed and scaled by its own standard error, unlike the unshrunken log2 fold change, and does not saturate into ties like a signed p-value. State this choice in the output
Feed fgsea the FULL ranked list of tested genes; never threshold before the preranked test
Gene set size window 15 to 500 applied AFTER intersecting each set with the tested genes
Run enrichment once per contrast; never pool genes from several contrasts into one list
Keep each collection separate — do not merge hallmark, Reactome-type and WikiPathways sets into one list, and adjust p-values within each collection
For any over-representation test the universe is exactly the genes tested in T1S2, never the whole genome or annotation
Do not run ORA on a list of fewer than about 50 significant genes; report the list size instead
Use human gene-set collections only — the store also holds mouse and rat collections and a species mismatch fails silently as an empty result
Set and record a random seed for the fgsea permutations
caveats: Enrichment results depend strongly on the method and the collection; report sets as hypotheses for follow-up, not as established findings
Gene length and expression level bias which genes reach significance in count data; the ranked test on the full list mitigates but does not remove this
With 4 subjects per group the ranked statistics are noisy, so weakly significant sets should be reported with that caveat attached
The treated_b vs treated_a ranked list may carry little signal if the two treatments act similarly; an empty result there is informative and must be reported as such

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on the full tested list is the default enrichment (R-0107), hallmark first then Reactome/WikiPathways for human (R-0048, R-0098, R-0165), one run per contrast (R-0104); the disputed ranking metric (R-0108) is settled in favour of the DESeq2 Wald statistic per R-0099.

steps.name: Integrated report
steps.question: What is the consolidated, reproducible answer: which genes respond to either treatment within subject, which are specific to treated_a or treated_b, do the two treatments differ, and how confident can the reader be given 4 subjects?
steps.description: Assemble the differential expression and enrichment outputs into one report. State the method, the package versions, the design formula ~ subject + condition, the reduced model ~ subject, control as the explicit reference level, all three named contrasts, the alpha and BH thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering out of 12,000, and the number of significant genes per contrast and for the LRT. Include the MA plot and the dispersion plot as fit diagnostics before any gene table. Gene tables carry the unshrunken log2FoldChange, the ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, and are ranked by the shrunken value. Include a heatmap of the top LRT genes on subject-centred VST values so the within-subject treatment effect is visible. Summarise the DESeq2/edgeR intersection from T1S3 as the high-confidence set. For enrichment, report the collection and its release, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, and the leading-edge genes of each significant set, with the caveat that enrichment results are method-dependent. Close with the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, random seeds, collection releases.
steps.context: Final synthesis across T1S2 (model), T1S3 (method overlap) and T2S1 (enrichment). The report is the artifact the user reads, so the power limits of a 4-subject design belong in it explicitly rather than in a footnote.
acceptance_criteria: Report states method, package versions, design formula, reduced model, reference level, every contrast by name, thresholds, number of genes tested and number significant per contrast
MA plot and dispersion plot included and placed before the gene tables, with a one-line reading of each
Gene tables carry log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, and are ranked by the shrunken value, not the unshrunken one
Heatmap of top LRT genes drawn on subject-centred VST values, showing the within-subject effect
DESeq2/edgeR overlap reported as the high-confidence set, with method-specific genes noted separately
Enrichment section names the collection and release, the ranking metric, the universe and the size window, lists leading-edge genes, and carries the method-dependence caveat
Reproducibility record attached with sessionInfo, package versions, seeds and collection releases
An explicit power statement: 4 subjects per condition, pairing recovers power by removing between-subject variance, and a null treated_b vs treated_a result is not evidence of equivalence
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep p-values from the unshrunken fit
Report the FDR as holding within each contrast, not across the set of contrasts
Do not present the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the result
Do not claim a mechanism from an enriched gene set; present sets as hypotheses
State the number of Cook's-distance-flagged NA genes separately from independent-filter NAs
caveats: No transcript-level data was provided, so nothing in this report addresses isoform switching

Blood transcriptomes are strongly shaped by cell composition; a differential gene may reflect a shift in cell proportions rather than a within-cell change, and this cannot be resolved from the gene-level matrix alone

grounding.reason: Report contents follow the procedure's report step: method/design/thresholds (R-0041), shrunken and unshrunken effects with ranking on the shrunken value (R-0085), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), two-method overlap (R-0042), enrichment provenance and leading edge (R-0051, R-0105), and the reproducibility record (R-0086).
